history.summary: Bijasan Mata Temple stands on Bijasan Tekri hill near Indore airport and is dedicated to Bijasan Mata, a fierce form of Goddess Durga; it houses nine forms of the Goddess and she is worshipped as the kuladevi of the Hindu Gadariya community. Most tourism sources say the current Maratha-style temple was built by Maharaja Shivajirao Holkar in 1760, but one detailed source dates construction to 1920 under Holkar patronage - and since Shivajirao Holkar reigned 1886-1903, the '1760' date is internally inconsistent (verify). Local tradition claims the hilltop shrine is nearly 1000 years old, once a forest site of tantra and siddhi practices where the idol sat on a stone platform; the priest notes a pond in the complex that never runs dry. A former Holkar hilltop guesthouse nearby now houses the Border Security Force Arms Museum. Newlywed couples widely visit seeking blessings for marriage and children, and grand fairs are held during Navaratri. Coordinates are approximate for the Tekri hilltop (verify on site).

town_description: Indore is the largest city and commercial capital of Madhya Pradesh, and was the capital of the Holkar dynasty under the Marathas. It blends historic landmarks like Rajwada palace and Lal Bagh Palace with a renowned food culture centred on Sarafa Bazaar. It has repeatedly been ranked India's cleanest city and is a major hub for education, trade, and tourism in central India.

travel.airport: Devi Ahilyabai Holkar International Airport, very close to Bijasan Tekri, ~3-4 km (verify)
travel.road: Steps and a motorable road lead up Bijasan Tekri; autos and cabs available from the city
